name: bench-harness-v3
description: RETIRED 2026-09-19 (manual attach only): not drain-runnable or superseded by lci-slice / lci-perf / lci-bench / lci-epic. Benchmark-harness slices (exploration S1-S5, edits S3.x) in lci-cpp, canonical trees benchmarks/repo-qa/{exploration,edits}. Supersedes bench-harness-v2, whose review-panel review_focus hard-coded S1 corpus-FORGE text (seed/tree-hash determinism) that fired verbatim on every unrelated slice — S3.1 bank, S3.2 conformance gate, S3.3 oracle gate, S3.4 runner, S3.5 scorer — steering reviewers at risks trivially absent from the diff (task 01KXPGREQ1ETNBWXEQ12M3TN2F). review_focus is now generalized to what holds for EVERY bench slice, with slice-specific risk left to the task's own acceptance criteria, and states acceptance-criteria-first precedence explicitly. Python-only: NO cmake/ctest gate (the C++ suite is irrelevant here and costs ~7min/gate — the Karpathy-rule-7 waste the test-perf epic exists to kill). Gate = hermetic stdlib-unittest suite under benchmarks/repo-qa/tests. NOTE: bench-unit-tests cwd defaults to the primary checkout; worktree-isolated lanes MUST pass an explicit cwd override to task_workflow_step_run / run_until_gate or the gate tests the wrong tree. MEASURED 2026-09-06 (task 01KXPZ3H9M2PADN15DRPR9ME74): dropping spec.cwd does NOT make the omission loud — the MCP host's own cwd IS /home/beagle/work/core/lci-cpp, so a no-override run still passes green against the primary checkout (572 tests) while the lane's worktree code (573 with its marker) goes unexecuted. Option (a) is falsified; a real fix must be (b) assert cwd against the lease's expected worktree, or (c) make the gate self-locating and refuse on a HEAD/branch mismatch. Review = worktrack-loop:worktrack-loop:review-context panel (doubled prefix is required for agent-type resolution in this workspace).

steps.name: review-panel
steps.specJson: {"subagent_type":"worktrack-loop:worktrack-loop:review-context","review_focus":"PRECEDENCE: gate on the task's own written acceptance criteria FIRST. This focus is supplementary steering, never a substitute for them, and never a reason to pass a slice whose criteria are unmet. If a risk named here is trivially absent from the diff, that is not evidence of a pass. Cross-cutting invariants that hold for EVERY bench-harness slice: (1) HERMETIC + DETERMINISTIC — fixtures must never clone or mutate the real repos; identical inputs must yield byte-identical outputs; no generated corpus content committed to git. (2) ORACLE INDEPENDENCE (.claude/rules/bench-harness-oracle-independence.md) — a validator sharing its matching mechanism (same regex/parser/helper code object) with the transformer it validates cannot catch that transformer's bugs; a validator with no proven failure case is unverified regardless of how many corpora it passes. Demand the discrimination test: re-inject the broken/untransformed form and assert the validator FAILS, plus confirm the good form PASSES. (3) NO SOLUTION LEAKAGE — the benchmark's reason to exist. No oracle path, symbol, identifier, or patch content reachable from any agent-visible prompt; leak linter green. (4) FAIL-CLOSED — explicit reason codes over silently-empty results or stub passes. (5) NO OVER-BUILD past a pinned reference stub. Slice-specific risk (e.g. forge seed/tree-hash byte-identity, which applies ONLY to the corpus-forge slice) belongs in that slice's acceptance criteria, NOT here."}

steps.name: acp-implement
steps.specJson:
{"agent": {"argv": ["opencode", "acp"]}, "model": "opencode-go/qwen3.8-flash", "permissions": "allow_all", "fs": "read_write", "prompt": "You are the implementer for work-track PERFORMANCE task {{task.id}} in workspace {{workspace}}.
Repository: /home/beagle/work/core/lci-cpp (C++20, CMake preset build/release, ccache). Read .claude/rules/*.md first; they are binding. Performance is judged against the theoretical ceiling named in the task, never against the previous version.

TASK: {{task.title}}

{{task.description}}

BUDGET: you have ONE hour of wall clock, and the before/after measurements are part of it. Read only what the task points at, then measure and start editing. A prior run on the sibling slice template spent the entire hour deriving a design and was killed having committed nothing. If you cannot finish, land and commit what you can prove and say plainly what you did not reach.

RULES:
- FIRST measure: run the measurement the task names on unchanged HEAD, record the numbers in a file under .worktrack/out/{{task.id}}-before.txt, and commit nothing yet. Then estimate the ceiling from the binding resource as the task instructs.
- Edit ONLY paths inside the task's file scope. Touching any other path fails the scope gate.
- Red-green: add a scaling-ratio test (relative, best-of-K; never absolute nanoseconds) that FAILS on HEAD for the complexity defect, then the fix, then green.
- Iterate with: cmake --build build/release --parallel --target lci_tests && ctest --test-dir build/release -R <Suite> -j4. Do NOT run the full suite; the gate runs it once after you.
- No allocation in inner loops, no mutex on read paths, sort before emit, no fallbacks, no catch(...) swallows. Delete replaced code.
- AFTER: re-run the same measurement, record .worktrack/out/{{task.id}}-after.txt, and put before/ceiling/after numbers in your final summary.
- Commit in atomic logical units with conventional-commit subjects (<type>(<scope>): <subject>, <=72 chars), body says WHY with the numbers. Stage files explicitly; never git add -A.
- TRAILER, EXACT SPELLING: end each commit message with this line, lowercase key, as part of the message's FINAL paragraph with no blank line before any Co-Authored-By that follows it:
    worktrack-task: {{task.id}}
  The scope gate finds your commits by this line. A blank line above it demotes it to body text; a different key spelling loses the commit.
- Stop with a short summary: commits, tests, before/ceiling/after numbers, anything unverified."}

steps.name: review-panel
steps.specJson: {"subagent_type":"worktrack-loop:review-context","review_focus":"Every performance claim anchors to a measured number from this run (.worktrack/out/<task>-before.txt / -after.txt, benchmark command_result) or to HEAD code at file:line; the ceiling estimate must be present and the after number compared to it, not to before. Task text is a hypothesis, not evidence. Do not re-run the suite or benchmark."}
